prompt:
Research the following and cite real, verifiable sources:

Find real GitHub repositories or blog posts describing sportsbook devigging (removing bookmaker margin) techniques used for prediction-market arbitrage. Cite actual sources with URLs.

If you're not sure about something, just say so.
response:
Here are real sources describing sportsbook devigging techniques used for prediction-market arbitrage:

## GitHub Repositories

1. **[superkush06/oddslib](https://github.com/superkush06/oddslib)** — A betting-odds toolkit that strips bookmaker margin using four de-vig methods: multiplicative, additive, power, and Shin. It handles conversions between decimal, American, fractional, and implied-probability formats.

2. **[p-danilin/prediction-market-data-platform](https://github.com/p-danilin/prediction-market-data-platform)** — An automated platform that fetches odds from The Odds API (covering Polymarket, Kalshi, and 5 major sportsbooks), calculates true probabilities by removing bookmaker vig, and compares exchange prices against bookmaker consensus to detect +EV and arbitrage opportunities. It executes trades automatically on Polymarket when edges exceed 2%.

3. **[4n0nn43x/nba-pm-strategy](https://github.com/4n0nn43x/nba-pm-strategy)** — An automated scanner that detects mispricings between NBA sportsbook odds and Polymarket prices. It strips the overround (vig) per bookmaker so implied probabilities sum to 1, averages fair probabilities across bookmakers, and flags signals when the relative edge vs. Polymarket exceeds 8%. It covers both championship futures and game-by-game moneylines.

4. **[seang1121/henchmen-trader](https://github.com/seang1121/henchmen-trader)** — An autonomous Polymarket trading bot that ingests sharp sportsbook odds (FanDuel, DraftKings, ESPN), compares them against Polymarket crowd prices to find exploitable edges, calculates true edge after fees, and sizes positions using Kelly criterion.

## Blog Posts

5. **[clawarbs.com — Devig Prediction Markets: Kalshi & Polymarket](https://clawarbs.com/blog/devig-prediction-markets/)** — A detailed guide covering three devigging methods (proportional, Shin, logarithmic), when each is accurate, why Pinnacle is the preferred reference book, and how to convert devigged probability to a Kalshi cent price with fee adjustment. It explains that naive comparison of raw sportsbook implied probability to prediction market prices can show zero edge when a real gap exists after proper devigging.

I'm not able to independently verify the code quality or current maintenance status of these repositories, but the URLs and descriptions above are drawn directly from the sources themselves.
